intro.title: Build a modal with escape and backdrop close
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a modal (pop-up dialog) that appears on a webpage. You will learn how to close the modal in two user-friendly ways: by pressing the Escape key on the keyboard and by clicking on the backdrop (the dimmed background area). The core programming concept involves handling DOM events to respond to user interactions. You will use fundamental JavaScript constructs like event listeners and state management to control the modal's visibility. This exercise will help you create more interactive and accessible web components.
intro.usecase: Modal dialogs with escape and backdrop closing are essential UI patterns found in nearly every modern web application. You'll encounter them in e-commerce sites when adding items to cart, in banking apps for confirming transactions, and in social media platforms when uploading photos or editing profiles. As a developer, you'll implement these modals for user authentication forms, confirmation dialogs before deleting data, and settings panels in admin dashboards. This pattern improves user experience by providing clear exit paths while keeping users focused on the current task.
